headline: Minnesota Wild's Major Investment In Kaprizov Already Paying Off In First Year Of Historic Contract
take:
Per The Hockey News, Kirill Kaprizov is already justifying the Minnesota Wild's investment in his eight-year extension, with the report suggesting he could earn some hardware to validate GM Bill Guerin's decision.

The numbers support the buzz, and there is some nuance. Kaprizov has 11 goals and 17 points in 10 games so far this season. His own expected goals (a measure of the quality of the chances he gets) sit at 7.57, so he is scoring about 3.43 goals above that mark. Some of that is finishing skill, but a gap that size usually cools, so the pace is unlikely to hold all year. What looks more durable is his impact: at five-on-five, MIN has 67 percent of the expected goals when he plays, and the team's share is about 21 percentage points better with him than without. His model projection of 1.62 expected goals per 60 minutes backs up a real scoring threat.

For MIN, the 6-2-2 record is helped by goaltending, with 4.7 goals saved above expected, while the team is 6.6 goals below expected offensively. Kaprizov is carrying much of the process.
